title: Home freeze test guide: small plastic bottle, water, freezer bag
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y7 lesson 10 (Home freeze test guide (portal): small plastic bottle, water, freezer bag)
intro: Lesson 10: How glaciers shape the land. To understand how glaciers erode rock by plucking, abrasion and freeze-thaw weathering

questions.a: Meltwater freezes onto rock; the glacier moves; the rock is pulled away
questions.model: Step 1: meltwater freezes onto the rock. Step 2: the glacier keeps moving. Step 3: it pulls the rock out. That is plucking.

questions.q: Why does freezing water break rock?
questions.a: Water expands when it freezes, pushing the crack wider
Rocks in the ice scrape and smooth the surface beneath

questions.q: Core: Draw a labelled cross-section of a glacier showing plucking, abrasion and freeze-thaw.
questions.a: Glacier with rocks in its base (abrasion), ice frozen onto rock at the back (plucking), cracked rock above (freeze-thaw)
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: draw the valley, the ice, then label 'abrasion: rocks in the ice scrape the floor' with an arrow.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain how the three processes work together (4 to 5 sentences).
questions.a: Freeze-thaw loosens rock above; plucking removes rock beneath; abrasion uses the rock to grind the valley; the ice carries it away

questions.q: Stretch: Freeze-thaw happens most where temperatures go above and below 0 °C often. Where in Britain might that be today?
questions.a: High mountains, such as the Scottish Highlands, in winter

questions.q: Big question: how can soft snow carve through solid rock?
questions.a: Snow becomes heavy moving ice that plucks rock, scrapes it by abrasion and is helped by freeze-thaw weathering
